en: The Glorious Hymn to Śiva as the Ninth Jewel (Śrīśivanavaratnastava)
Bṛhaspati [offers salutations] to the God who removes all obstacles, the wielder of the great illusion and the trident; to the ascetic, the Great Lord, the bestower of the knowledge of reality.
(1) Salutations to the one clad in the girdle of muñja grass, to the Pure One; salutations to the embodiment of compassion; salutations to the God of gods, the giver of the Vedānta. (2)
Salutations to the Supreme Rudra, the one who brings us safely across; salutations again and again. Salutations to You, the Great Lord whose form is the universe, the support of all existence.
(3) Salutations to the stainless Self, the cause of the destruction of the suffering of devotees. Salutations to You, the Death of Death, Time itself, and that which transcends time.
(4) Salutations to You, the eternal conqueror of the senses and the subduer of anger. Salutations to the breaker of heresy; salutations to the remover of sin. (5)

Salutations to the Lord of the daughter of the king of mountains; salutations to the bliss of yoga, to yoga itself, and to the Lord of yogis. (6) Salutations to you, the protector of the vital breaths for those devoted to *prāṇāyāma*; salutations to the one who has entered the *mūlādhāra*, whose nature is the fundamental light. (7) Salutations to the one who has entered the bulb of the navel, who dwells in the region of the heart; salutations to the Supreme Self, manifest as the fullness of Being-Consciousness-Bliss. (8) Salutations to Śiva, whose prowess is wondrous; salutations to Śiva, whose form is wondrous.
Salutations to Śiva, the leader of all; salutations to Śiva, the cause of immortality; salutations!
(9) Sūta said: He who constantly recites this hymn with devotion and self-restraint, for him liberation shall be within his grasp, because it is dear to Śaṅkara. (10)
The seeker of knowledge obtains knowledge; the seeker of marriage becomes a householder; and the seeker of dispassion attains that dispassion which delivers one from worldly existence.
Therefore, day by day, with concentrated minds, you should recite this hymn for the sake of destroying worldly existence, for it is the destroyer of worldly existence.
Thus ends the "Hymn of the Nine Jewels of Śiva" composed by Bṛhaspati in the Sūta-saṃhitā of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.
